{{Top}}
{{Quote|What good is all your uncle's work if it's taken over by the Empire?...You know they're starting to nationalize commerce in the central systems...it won't be long before your uncle is merely a tenant, slaving for the greater glory of the Empire.|[[Biggs Darklighter/Legends|Biggs Darklighter]]|<ref name="Star Wars Episode IV: A New Hope (novel)">[[Star Wars: A New Hope (novelization)|''Star Wars Episode IV: A New Hope'' novelization]]</ref>}}
[[File:EmperorsArrival-RotJAVA.png|thumb|250px|[[Galactic Emperor/Legends|Emperor]] [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine]], tyrannical ruler of the galaxy.]]

'''Imperialization''' or '''nationalization''' were terms for the process by which the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]] established a system of control over the individual, instructions, commercial enterprise, or [[Planet/Legends|planets]], and tight coordination over all aspects of society and commerce.

==Overview==
{{Quote|The Jedi Order is a lesson to us that we cannot permit any agency to become powerful enough to pose a threat to our designs, or the freedoms we enjoy. That is why it is essential we increase and centralize our military, both to preserve the peace and to protect the Empire against inevitable attempts at insurrection. To that end I have already ordered the production of new classes of capital ships and starfighters, suitable for command by nonclone officers and crew, who themselves will be the product of Imperial academies, made up of candidates drawn from existing star system flight schools. No less important, our present army of clone troopers is aging at an accelerating rate, and will need to be supplemented, gradually replaced, by new batches of clones.|[[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine]]|<ref name="Dark Lord: The Rise of Darth Vader">''[[Dark Lord: The Rise of Darth Vader]]''</ref>}}
[[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine's]] desire for control required the elimination of all other forms of influence, especially the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]]. The period following the [[Declaration of a New Order]] was characterized by the systematic elimination of Galactic Republic organizations that could potentially influence people. All the institutions of the Old Republic found themselves either dismantled or changed beyond recognition.

The Imperialization also included the formation of various organizations with membership for segments of the population, in particular the youth. The [[Commission for the Preservation of the New Order/Legends|Commission for the Preservation of the New Order]] (COMPNOR) was created as an umbrella organization for those groups that were designed to maintain support for Emperor Palpatine's [[New Order/Legends|New Order]].

==Specific measures==
{{Quote|Half the budget is going to the production of these enormous Star Destroyers. He's having new stormtroopers grown. And that's not the worst of it. The Finance Committee can't even account for some of the spending.|[[Mon Mothma/Legends|Mon Mothma]]|<ref name="Dark Lord: The Rise of Darth Vader" />}}
In a more specific sense, Imperialization refers to the measures taken by the Empire to strengthen its control over the galaxy.

The [[Coruscant sector/Legends|Coruscant sector]] was renamed the Imperial Sector, [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]] itself was renamed Imperial Center, and [[Galactic City/Legends|Galactic City]] was renamed Imperial City. The [[Galactic Senate/Legends|Galactic Senate]] was reorganized into the [[Imperial Senate/Legends|Imperial Senate]]. The [[Grand Army of the Republic/Legends|Grand Army of the Republic]] became the [[Imperial Army/Legends|Imperial Army]], and the [[Republic Navy/Legends|Republic Navy]] became the [[Imperial Navy/Legends|Imperial Navy]]. The [[Special Operations Brigade/Legends|Special Operations Brigade]] was terminated and its elite [[Clone commando/Legends|clone commandos]] and [[Advanced Recon Commando/Legends|ARC troopers]] reorganized into the [[Imperial Commando Special Unit]], itself part of [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Lord Vader's]] [[501st Legion/Legends|501st Legion]]. The four decrepit intelligence agencies of the Republic were merged into [[Imperial Intelligence/Legends|Imperial Intelligence]]. The Grand Army mainframe and Republic networks at large were overhauled, and everything from data flow to communications were given entirely new interfaces with new coding and new passwords.<ref name="RepCom Order 66">''[[Order 66: A Republic Commando Novel]]''</ref> The [[Imperial Palace/Legends|Palace of the Republic]] was rebuilt and expanded, becoming the [[Imperial Palace/Legends|Imperial Palace]], eclipsing all other buildings on Imperial Center.

[[File:ImperialSuppression-TCGDoH.jpg|thumb|left|250px|The [[Imperial-class Star Destroyer/Legends|''Imperial''-class Star Destroyer]] was a symbol of Imperialization]]
Vast resources and quintillions of [[Galactic Credit Standard/Legends|credits]] were dedicated to expanding the [[Imperial Military/Legends|Imperial Military]] and to funding new scientific developments.<ref name="Dark Empire Sourcebook">''[[Dark Empire Sourcebook]]''</ref> This military buildup eventually resulted in the [[Imperial Navy/Legends|Imperial Navy]] fielding millions of starships, the [[Imperial Army/Legends|Imperial Army]] being comprised of tens of trillions of soldiers, and the creation of a vast force of [[Stormtrooper/Legends|stormtroopers]].<ref name="Rebellion Era Campaign Guide">''[[Rebellion Era Campaign Guide]]''</ref> Major scientific breakthroughs and advances during the [[Imperial Era/Legends|Imperial Period]] included, but were not limited to, new [[Superweapon/Legends|superweapons]], [[Gravity well projector/Legends|gravity well projectors]], [[Cloaking device/Legends|cloaking devices]], and [[Hypermatter reactor/Legends|hypermatter annihilators]].<ref name="Dark Empire Sourcebook" />

Palpatine deployed one [[Moff/Legends|Moff]] in each sector. These officers were supposed to efficiently govern individual sectors and regions of the Empire. Though Imperial [[Governor/Legends|governors]] and Moffs were dispatched to oversee many of the planets and sectors of [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]], they largely maintained a policy of non-interference with respect to local politics.<ref name="Imperial Sourcebook">[[Imperial Sourcebook (Second Edition)|''Imperial Sourcebook'', Second Edition]]</ref> The vast majority of the planets within the Empire maintained their own sovereign governments and everyday life for an average citizen was not very different from the days of the Galactic Republic, especially for those who strongly supported the [[New Order/Legends|New Order]]. However, if the Empire desired to obtain resources from a particular planet it would not hesitate to take it by force. Planets which had their governments entirely supplanted by an Imperial governor were usually [[Alien/Legends|Non-Human]] or those who supported the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Alliance to Restore the Republic]].<ref name="The Force Unleashed Campaign Guide">''[[The Force Unleashed Campaign Guide]]''</ref><ref name="Rebellion Era Campaign Guide" /> Additionally, the planets located between the least restrictive areas of the galaxy, the [[Core Worlds/Legends|Core Worlds]] and [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim territories]], bore the brunt of Imperial authority and scrutiny. Overall, less than one in 80 planets experienced some sort of modification to their local governmental procedures or had members of a ruling body removed from office to better conform to the will of the Empire.<ref name="Imperial Sourcebook" /> Other planets which were discontent with Imperial rule were kept in line with the [[Tarkin Doctrine/Legends|Tarkin Doctrine]] of "rule by fear of force rather than force itself" although if the threat alone failed then actual force would most certainly be used.

There were also certain increases in the state control and centralization of economic procedures. This included the nationalization of commercial enterprises like the [[Trade Federation/Legends|Trade Federation]], the [[Techno Union/Legends|Techno Union]], the [[Commerce Guild/Legends|Commerce Guild]], the [[Corporate Alliance/Legends|Corporate Alliance]], the [[Hyper-Communications Cartel/Legends|Hyper-Communications Cartel]], and other commerce within the Empire. In addition, one of the first actions of the Empire was, upon nominating [[Gahg]] to [[Finance Minister|Minister of Finance]], to completely annex the seized holdings of various defeated Separatist worlds, which had been nearly completed a few months later.<ref name="Dark Times 1: The Path to Nowhere, Part 1">[[Dark Times 1|''Dark Times'' 1]]</ref> The [[InterGalactic Banking Clan/Legends|InterGalactic Banking Clan]] managed to avoid the fate of its co-conspirators and wasn't completely shut down, though the Empire exerted a considerable degree of control over it. The Empire would also go on to nationalize the [[Fondor Shipyards/Legends|Fondor Shipyards]] around the time of the [[Battle of Yavin/Legends|Battle of Yavin]]. This was due to complications involving the construction of the [[Star Dreadnought/Legends|Star Dreadnought]] [[Executor/Legends|''Executor'']], though the [[Fondor Guild of Starshipwrights]] would remain in place to oversee the project.<ref name="The Essential Atlas">''[[The Essential Atlas]]''</ref>

The Empire continued to nationalize some corporate entities, but such actions were primarily reserved for those companies which were part of or supported the [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|Confederacy of Independent Systems]], and later those which favored and aided the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebellion]]. The Empire did assume direct control over some of the spoils of war from the Separatists, but most of the assets were actually given over to [[Loyalist/Legends|loyalist]] companies such as [[Kuat Drive Yards/Legends|Kuat Drive Yards]], [[Santhe/Sienar Technologies|Sienar Systems]], [[Tagge Company/Legends|TaggeCo.]], and [[Merr-Sonn Munitions, Inc./Legends|Merr-Sonn]].<ref name="Republic HoloNet News Special Inaugural Edition 16:5:24">{{InsiderCite|84|Republic HoloNet News Special Inaugural Edition 16:5:241}}</ref><ref name="The Force Unleashed Campaign Guide" /> Unless they acted in opposition to its interests, the Empire largely left loyal companies alone and even expanded the territory of the [[Corporate Sector Authority/Legends|Corporate Sector Authority]] to encompass 30,000 star systems.<ref name="HSATCSSB">''[[Han Solo and the Corporate Sector Sourcebook]]''</ref>
